blocks.text: Badenoch says it's 'disturbing' that Xi, Trump and Putin look like they're 'trying to carve up world between them'
Alexandra Topping
Alexandra Topping is a Guardian political correspondent.

Kemi Badenoch was in a straight-talking mode on the media round this morning, calling the historic meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin “disturbing”, saying it looked like they were trying to “carve” up the world” between them.
Speaking on the Today programme, the leader of the opposition said the meeting was “absolutely not reassuring”.
She said:

double quotation markThere are three world leaders who look like they’re trying to carve up the world between them, a tri-polar world where Xi gets Asia, America gets the western hemisphere and Russia gets Europe, and that is very concerning, especially seeing Donald Trump call President Putin his friend. Russia is not America’s friend, it certainly hasn’t been during my lifetime. But also at a time when we’re all worried about where the Ukraine war is going, the message that is sending to President Zelensky and of course the other summit that is taking place … is very concerning indeed. And what I want to know is where we fit in in all of this. I don’t want to be in a polarised world run by Russia. I’ll do everything I can to make sure that doesn’t happen.

Badenoch went further than the prime minister, who was asked about the meeting by Ed Davey at prime minister’s questions yesterday. The Liberal Democrat leader said “the security implications of Trump, Putin and Xi cosying up” should highlight the need for a fresh deal with the European Union.

Burnham replied that he would be in Berlin for a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing to support Ukraine in China, but stopped short of expressing concern about the meeting of the three world leaders.
He said:

double quotation markThe thing that we need to do is continue to stand squarely by Ukraine and that is what this government will do. And on this issue, I do pay tribute to all sides of the house because that is what we’ve managed to do in the years since the conflict began and that is the right thing to do … Let that clear message go out as that meeting takes place in [China] – this country is squarely with Ukraine.

blocks.text: Badenoch says using amputee athletes to justify cutting disability benefits was ‘message of hope’

Good morning. At PMQs yesterday Andy Burnham said that Kemi Badenoch should withdraw the “double amputees run marathons” comment that she used to justify the Tory plan to cut sickness and disability benefits by £14bn. It was “crass and insensitive”, he said.
This morning Badenoch defended what she was saying claimed that, in fact, she was delivering a “message of hope”.
In an interview on the Today programme, asked if she accepted that her remark was insensitive, Badenoch said she didn’t. She went on:

double quotation markI will speak the truth and I will say what I believe is common sense. And what I know is that, if people can work, then we should encourage them to work. And what I’m saying is actually a message of hope, that if people even with significant, problems can work, then those who have ADHD and mild anxiety should go to work.

When the presenter, Nick Robinson, put it to her that it was unreasonable to use an exceptional case as a guide to what most disabled people should be doing, Badenoch did not agree. “We do use extreme examples to illustrate things,” she said.

Robinson tried again, saying she was taking “one extreme case [to] imply that anybody on disability benefits should just get on with it”. Badenoch accused him of “faux outrage” and “tone policing”. She added:
double quotation markPeople are free to disagree, but they know where I’m coming from. I will post more from the interview shortly.
Today the news will be dominated by two summits. This afternoon Burnham is in Berlin for a meeting of the pro-Ukraine coalition of the willing. We have coverage of this on our Europe live blog.
And in China, Vladimir Putin, who invaded Ukraine, Xi Jinping, his leading ally, and Donald Trump, who is seen by many as a closet Putin ally, are meeting now. You can read about that here.

We will have comments open in about an hour. That is because I will be doing a Q&A this afternoon, probably from about 3pm, and I will try to answer as many questions as possible. Do post them below the line.
Here is the agenda for the day.
9.30am: Louise Haigh, the first secretary of state and Cabinet Office minister, takes questions in the Commons.

10am: The Conservative party announces the results of the first round of voting in the election of its candidate for London mayor for 2028. James Cleverly, the former home secretary and former foreign secretary, is expected to get more than 50% of the vote, meaning a second round of voting should not be necessary.
11.30am: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.
Noon: Heather Hallett, the Covid inquiry chair, publishes her report on the test, trace and isolate system.

Around 12.15pm (UK time): Andy Burnham arrives in Berlin for a meeting of the pro-Ukraine coalition of the willing. He is expected to speak to the media later in the afternoon after the plenary has finished.
1pm: Chris Bryant, the Northern Ireland secretary, attends a meeting of the British-Irish Intergovernmental Conference in Dublin.
